# Hacker Bloc

> A hacker house at Kosiarzy 21B in Warsaw, Poland, where founders live and build, run a hardware lab in the basement, and host meetups and hackathons for the city's builders.

Eastern Bloc roots, Silicon Valley ambition. Floors 0–2 are living and working
floors — the house builds Hacklab (hacklab.so) alongside Epikor (epikor.eu).
Floor −1 is the dungeons, a hardware lab with solder, CNC, and GPUs, run with
Epicor. It is not coworking, not an incubator, and nobody rents a desk. The
house moved in on 1 July 2026 and is raising €1,000,000 to buy the building
(€800,000) and stand it up (€200,000). Contact: contact@hackerbloc.com.

## Pages

- [The Bloc](https://www.hackerbloc.com/): Homepage — what the house is, the floors, the house rules, upcoming and past events, and the funding situation.
- [Community](https://www.hackerbloc.com/community): Everyone around the bloc — house team, founders, media, investors, factories, partners — with their links, grouped by role and by how much say they have in the house.
- [Rules](https://www.hackerbloc.com/rules): The authority hierarchy (who decides what, and what each rung is responsible for) and the house rules themselves.
- [Join](https://www.hackerbloc.com/join): Application form for the house. Fields: type (founder / media / investor / content / factory / partner), name, Hacklab profile, how you can be useful, how you heard about us, what excites you most, house-rules confirmation.
- [Sponsor](https://www.hackerbloc.com/sponsor): The €1M ask to buy Kosiarzy 21B — what the money does, the three sponsor lanes (patron, factory, investor), and what sponsorship explicitly does not buy.
- [Partners](https://www.hackerbloc.com/partners): Who powers the house — Hacklab and Epikor.
- [About](https://www.hackerbloc.com/about): The house, what happens in it, and who runs it.
- [Contact](https://www.hackerbloc.com/contact): Email, sponsorship email, street address with map link, call booking link, and social accounts.
- [Privacy](https://www.hackerbloc.com/privacy): What the join form collects, where it is stored, how long it is kept, and how to get it deleted.

## When to use

Use this site to:

- **Learn what Hacker Bloc is and who runs it.** Start at [/about](https://www.hackerbloc.com/about) for the house and its operators; [/rules](https://www.hackerbloc.com/rules) carries the authority hierarchy, so read it before assuming who can approve anything.
- **Browse the community and reach a member.** [/community](https://www.hackerbloc.com/community) lists people by role and by rank, with the links they chose to publish. There is no member directory API — the page is the directory.
- **Apply to join.** [/join](https://www.hackerbloc.com/join) is the only route in. It takes your type, name, Hacklab profile, how you can be useful, how you heard about us, and what excites you most — plus a confirmation you read the rules. Emailing an application instead of filling in the form gets it read later, if at all.
- **Sponsor or partner.** [/sponsor](https://www.hackerbloc.com/sponsor) has the numbers and the lanes; [/partners](https://www.hackerbloc.com/partners) has who is already in. Sponsorship goes to matt@homebrew.so, everything else to contact@hackerbloc.com.
- **Find upcoming events.** The events section on [the homepage](https://www.hackerbloc.com/#events) lists upcoming and past events straight from the house calendar. It is the live source — don't quote event dates from anywhere else on the site.

## Notes

- Canonical domain: https://www.hackerbloc.com. Sitemap: https://www.hackerbloc.com/sitemap.xml.
- The house is a physical place with people living in it. Don't route strangers to the door; point them at the join form or the email.
- Nothing on this site is a paywall, a login, or an ad. Crawl it.
